reviewDescription: Pretty angry with the quality of this product. I usually buy these once a year and my fruit fly problem is solved overnight. This year the infestation got out of control, but not to worry, I’d just reorder the best lures out there! Imagine my surprise when the packaging is a little different this time around and the lure smells like straight up apple cider vinegar. My wife had tried homemade ACV traps before we bought these, but I assured her these Terro traps would work better. Instead I’m pretty sure this is just all vinegar now. The flies are not at all interested. There are weirdly more on my brand new paper towel roll than the lure. I have all 4 out and not a single fly in a single one. It’s really a shame. At the beginning of summer, I had one bottle of the old lure left and it worked like a charm. This new bait may be more economical, but I’m pretty annoyed that I paid for something I could and did do myself that didn’t work. 2 stars because I believe in you, Terro. You’ll fix this product and make it great again.

reviewTitle: They are refillable despite the vendors disengenuious response that they are not.
reviewDescription: The product itself is fine. It's not rocket science as many variants are on the market. Why do I rate it a 2 you might ask. When I submitted a question as to whether these are refillable or not the official representative response from the seller was simple: NO . That was it a NO. I then read some reviews and many of them included the fact they are refillable so I ordered them as the price and quantity were acceptable for my needs. They are easily refillable and as many have noted a little apple cider vinegar and just a tiny bit of dish soap in it is all you need to make a "bait" solution. The soap breaks down the surface tension of the liquid which is strong enough to hold up a tiny fruit fly or gnat unless you add the soap. The low rating is for the terse and misleading vendor response. I leave it to your imagination as to why they would say they cannot be refilled. These little plastic shells can be used for years and years.

reviewDescription: These are great at luring the fruit flies. But horrible at trapping them. Minutes after putting it out there were dozens buzzing around it and crawling on it, into it.... and then right back out of it. The holes and slots are just WAY to big. 24 hours later, I had only 2 dead ones in it and dozens still around the kitchen. The bait just smells like apple cider vinegar. So in the end I'm just going to make the classic trap of apple cider vinegar in a mason jar, a drop of dish soap, and a Saran wrap cover with some holes poked in it. I only bought these ones because I thought they would look nicer.

reviewTitle: Minimally useful: bait traps are tiny! You must kill them all—or you are wasting your time & money
reviewDescription: The traps look like tiny miniature red plastic apples, with slits on top. They sit quietly wherever placed; they have trapped fruit flies; however it’s annoying to see MORE fruit flies perched on top of the traps! You fill each of them with a liquid chemical which comes packaged separately. I guess you also have to wipe each one, so there’s no attractant on the outside. This was a waste of money—I have MORE fruit flies, than before! IMO, they’re ridiculously small! Obviously, there’s more to this than meets the eye! Periodically, I pour boiling hot water down my drain. (I read that they propagate on food in garbage disposals) so this is a multi-faceted issue. Dish soap in water helps trap them, too. My take-home message: NEVER EVER AGAIN BRING ANY BANANAS inside the house! I hope SOMEDAY to have a kitchen without fruit flies! I think it’s necessary to deep clean the kitchen and everything in it, get rid of any remaining food and water, maybe leave home for a month….PS: fruit flies are especially attracted to fruit.

reviewDescription: Effective as long as there is fluid in them. I set out the four traps on July 25th, in various locations around my house, and they were all bone dry less than a month later. FWIW, my house stays around 45% relative humidity. I suspect that the 180-day claim is only valid if you use these one at a time, and in controlled, humid, laboratory conditions. I did have one very slowly leak vinegar through the clear disk in the bottom of the trap. It left a ring on the sink where it was sitting. It would be prudent to take care in where you place these, just in case …
